items.name: Compliance Program
items.summary: Establishes the formal governance framework for the enterprise compliance function, ensuring compliance obligations across all insurance lines are documented, overseen at the Board level, and periodically evaluated for effectiveness.

subs.title: Written Compliance Program
subs.description: A formal, documented compliance program must be maintained that defines the program's scope, governance structure, key compliance obligations across P&C, Life & Retirement, and group benefits lines, and the roles responsible for execution. The document is approved by the Chief Compliance Officer and updated whenever material regulatory or organizational changes occur.

subs.title: Board Oversight
subs.description: The Board of Directors, or a designated committee, exercises documented oversight of the compliance program, including approving the program charter and receiving regular reports on compliance posture, significant matters, and resource adequacy. Minutes must evidence the Board's review and any direction given to management.

subs.title: Annual Effectiveness Review
subs.description: An evaluation of the compliance program's design and operating effectiveness is performed at least annually, assessing coverage of regulatory obligations, adequacy of staffing and tooling, and outcomes of testing and issue remediation. Results and recommended enhancements are reported to senior management and the Board.

items.name: Compliance Testing
items.summary: Governs the independent testing of compliance controls so that gaps in adherence to regulatory and policy requirements are detected systematically rather than discovered by regulators or through consumer harm.

subs.title: Risk-Based Testing Plan
subs.description: Compliance testing coverage is determined by a documented risk assessment that weighs regulatory exposure, prior findings, business volume, and recent change in each area, with higher-risk processes such as claims handling and producer licensing tested more frequently and in greater depth. The plan and its risk rationale are approved by the Chief Compliance Officer annually.

subs.title: Testing Calendar
subs.description: A forward-looking calendar schedules each test engagement across the year, identifying the business area, scope, assigned tester, and target completion date. The calendar is maintained centrally, and deferrals or scope changes require documented approval so coverage commitments remain visible.

subs.title: Findings Tracked
subs.description: Every testing exception is logged in the compliance issue register with a severity rating, accountable owner, remediation plan, and due date. Open findings are monitored to closure, with aging and overdue items escalated to compliance leadership and reflected in management reporting.

items.name: Compliance Training
items.summary: Ensures the workforce understands the regulatory and ethical obligations relevant to their work, maintaining a trained employee base that regulators and auditors can verify through completion evidence.

subs.title: Annual Compliance Training
subs.description: All employees and contingent workers complete a core compliance curriculum at least once per year covering topics such as privacy, anti-fraud, unfair trade practices, and reporting obligations. New hires receive the training within a defined onboarding window before assuming regulated duties.

subs.title: Role-Specific Modules
subs.description: Supplemental training is assigned based on job function, so that claims adjusters, underwriters, producers, and customer-facing staff receive instruction on the regulations and conduct standards specific to their roles, such as fair claims settlement practices or suitability rules for annuity sales. Module assignments are reviewed when an employee changes roles.

subs.title: Completion Tracking
subs.description: Training assignments, completions, and assessment results are recorded in the learning management system, with automated reminders for approaching deadlines and escalation to managers for past-due items. Completion rates are reported to compliance leadership and retained as evidence for regulatory examinations.

items.name: Risk Appetite Statement
items.summary: Defines the enterprise's formally approved boundaries for risk-taking, giving business units a clear, Board-sanctioned reference for how much underwriting, investment, operational, and strategic risk the carrier is willing to accept.

subs.title: Board-Approved Risk Appetite
subs.description: The enterprise risk appetite statement must be formally approved by the Board of Directors, articulating the types and aggregate level of risk the carrier will accept in pursuit of its strategy across underwriting, market, credit, operational, and reputational dimensions. Material amendments require re-approval rather than management-level revision.

subs.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Limits
subs.description: The appetite statement is operationalized through measurable limits, such as capital-at-risk thresholds, catastrophe exposure ceilings, and counterparty concentration caps, alongside qualitative expressions for risks that resist quantification, such as conduct and reputational risk. Tolerances and limit breaches are defined so monitoring against appetite is objective.

subs.title: Reviewed Annually
subs.description: The risk appetite statement is reviewed at least once per year against the current strategic plan, capital position, and external environment, with the review and any resulting changes documented and presented to the Board. Off-cycle reviews are triggered by significant events such as acquisitions or major shifts in market conditions.

items.name: Risk Assessment
items.summary: Standardizes how identified risks are measured and visualized across the enterprise, producing a consistent, comparable view of exposure that supports prioritization of mitigation effort and capital decisions.

subs.title: Likelihood and Impact Scoring
subs.description: Each risk in the enterprise inventory is scored on standardized likelihood and impact scales with defined rating criteria, including financial, regulatory, operational, and reputational impact dimensions. Scoring definitions are calibrated so ratings are comparable across business units and risk categories.

subs.title: Inherent and Residual Risk
subs.description: Risks are assessed both on an inherent basis, before considering controls, and on a residual basis after evaluating control design and effectiveness, making the value of the control environment explicit. Residual ratings that exceed appetite trigger documented treatment decisions.

subs.title: Heat Maps Maintained
subs.description: Assessment results are maintained in heat map form plotting likelihood against impact for the enterprise and for each major business segment, refreshed on the established assessment cycle. Heat maps accompany risk reporting so leadership and the Board can see concentration and movement of top risks at a glance.

items.name: Risk Identification
items.summary: Ensures the enterprise maintains a complete and current picture of the risks it faces, so that no material exposure to the carrier's underwriting, investment, or operational footprint goes unrecognized.

subs.title: Annual Risk Assessment
subs.description: A structured enterprise-wide risk identification exercise is conducted at least annually, engaging business unit leaders, risk owners, and subject matter experts across P&C, Life & Retirement, and group benefits operations to surface new and changed risks. Results feed the risk inventory and the assessment and reporting processes.

subs.title: Emerging Risks Monitored
subs.description: A defined process scans for emerging risks such as climate-driven loss trends, AI and model risk, cyber threats, and shifting regulatory expectations, drawing on industry sources, regulator publications, and internal indicators. Candidate emerging risks are evaluated for relevance and, where warranted, formally added to the inventory with an assigned owner.

subs.title: Risk Inventory Maintained
subs.description: A central inventory records every identified risk with its description, category, owner, current ratings, and linkage to controls and mitigation plans. The inventory is the authoritative source for risk reporting and is updated as risks are added, re-rated, or retired.

items.name: Risk Mitigation
items.summary: Governs how the enterprise responds to risks that exceed appetite, ensuring treatments are documented, progress is visible, and named individuals are answerable for bringing exposure back within tolerance.

subs.title: Control Activities Documented
subs.description: Controls that mitigate each material risk are formally documented, describing the control objective, how the control operates, its frequency, and the evidence it produces. Documentation is kept current so control effectiveness can be assessed and relied upon in residual risk ratings.

subs.title: Action Plans Tracked
subs.description: Where residual risk exceeds tolerance, remediation action plans are recorded with defined milestones, target dates, and required resources, and progress is tracked through the ERM system. Slipping or stalled plans are escalated through risk committee reporting until completed or formally re-scoped.

subs.title: Risk Owners Accountable
subs.description: Every material risk has a named owner at an appropriate level of seniority who is responsible for the accuracy of the risk's assessment, the adequacy of its controls, and the delivery of its action plans. Ownership assignments are reviewed when organizational changes occur so accountability never lapses.

items.name: Risk Reporting
items.summary: Defines the cadence and escalation discipline for communicating the enterprise risk profile, keeping management and the Board informed in time to act before exposures crystallize into losses or regulatory issues.

subs.title: Monthly Risk Dashboard
subs.description: A risk dashboard is produced each month for senior management summarizing key risk indicators, limit utilization against appetite, top and emerging risks, and the status of significant mitigation plans. Metrics are sourced from the risk inventory and operational systems so the dashboard reflects current data rather than narrative alone.

subs.title: Quarterly Board Report
subs.description: The Chief Risk Officer delivers a quarterly report to the Board or its risk committee covering the enterprise risk profile relative to appetite, material changes since the prior quarter, stress and scenario results where applicable, and matters requiring Board attention. The report and the Board's discussion are documented in committee records.

subs.title: Escalation Triggers Defined
subs.description: Objective thresholds specify when a risk event, limit breach, or indicator deterioration must be escalated outside the normal reporting cycle, including to whom and within what timeframe. Triggers are documented in the ERM framework and tested periodically so escalation operates reliably under stress.

items.name: Code of Conduct
items.summary: Maintains the enterprise code of conduct as a living obligation rather than a shelf document, ensuring every employee affirms, understands, and can access the behavioral standards expected of an insurance carrier's workforce.

subs.title: Annual Acknowledgment
subs.description: Each employee, officer, and director formally acknowledges the code of conduct every year, attesting that they have read it, understand it, and have disclosed any matters it requires. Acknowledgments are captured electronically with completion monitored and non-responders escalated to management.

subs.title: Training Required
subs.description: Training on the code of conduct is mandatory for all personnel, reinforcing key provisions such as fair treatment of policyholders, anti-bribery expectations, confidentiality, and the duty to report suspected misconduct. Content is refreshed periodically and incorporated into new-hire onboarding before access to sensitive systems or customer data is granted.

subs.title: Available in Multiple Languages
subs.description: The code of conduct is published in the primary languages of the workforce so that comprehension is not limited by English proficiency, with translations maintained in step with each revision of the English master. Accessibility of all language versions is verified on the company intranet and in onboarding materials.

items.name: Conflicts of Interest
items.summary: Governs the identification and management of personal and organizational conflicts so that decisions about underwriting, claims, vendors, and investments are made in the interest of the company and its policyholders rather than private benefit.

subs.title: Annual Disclosure
subs.description: All employees, officers, and directors complete a conflicts of interest disclosure at least annually, declaring outside business activities, financial interests, family relationships with vendors or competitors, and any other circumstances that could impair objectivity. Material changes arising mid-year must be disclosed promptly rather than held for the next cycle.

subs.title: Review Process
subs.description: Submitted disclosures are reviewed by the compliance function against defined criteria, with potentially significant conflicts referred to the ethics committee or designated senior officer for determination. Review outcomes and their rationale are documented and retained.

subs.title: Mitigation Plans
subs.description: Where a disclosed conflict cannot simply be eliminated, a written mitigation plan specifies the safeguards applied, such as transferring duties, restricting information access, or adding independent oversight to affected decisions. Plans are monitored for adherence and revisited when the underlying circumstances change.

subs.title: Recusal Requirements
subs.description: Individuals with a conflict must recuse themselves from decisions, approvals, and deliberations the conflict touches, including vendor selection, claims determinations, hiring, and investment actions. Recusals are documented in the relevant decision record so the integrity of the outcome can be demonstrated afterward.

items.name: Whistleblower Program
items.summary: Provides a trusted mechanism for surfacing suspected misconduct, ensuring concerns from any level of the organization can be raised safely and are investigated with rigor and consistency.

subs.title: Anonymous Reporting Channel
subs.description: A reporting channel operated by an independent third party is available around the clock by phone and web, allowing employees, contractors, and producers to raise concerns anonymously in their preferred language. The channel's existence and access details are publicized through training, the intranet, and workplace postings.

subs.title: Non-Retaliation Policy
subs.description: A formal policy prohibits retaliation in any form against individuals who report concerns in good faith or participate in investigations, with violations treated as serious misconduct subject to discipline up to termination. Reporters who allege retaliation receive a separate, prioritized review.

subs.title: Investigation Protocol
subs.description: Reported matters follow a documented protocol covering intake triage, severity classification, assignment to qualified investigators, evidence handling, confidentiality safeguards, and timeframes for resolution. Outcomes, substantiation rates, and significant matters are reported to the audit committee, and case records are retained per the retention schedule.

items.name: Claims Handling Standards
items.summary: Sets the conduct requirements for adjudicating policyholder claims so that handling across all lines withstands market conduct examination and delivers the fair, prompt treatment state insurance laws demand.

subs.title: Unfair Claims Practices Compliance
subs.description: Claims operations must conform to the unfair claims settlement practices acts of every state in which the carrier writes business, including prohibitions on misrepresenting policy provisions, compelling litigation through lowball offers, and failing to act in good faith on claims where liability is clear. Procedures, adjuster guidance, and quality reviews are mapped to these statutory requirements.

subs.title: Timing Requirements
subs.description: Acknowledgment of claims, requests for information, coverage decisions, and payment issuance must each occur within the timeframes prescribed by applicable state regulations, applying the strictest standard where the company elects a uniform internal benchmark. Cycle times are monitored and aged claims are escalated before regulatory deadlines are breached.

subs.title: Documentation
subs.description: Each claim file must contain a complete record of the investigation, correspondence, evaluation rationale, reserve changes, and settlement basis, sufficient for an independent reviewer or market conduct examiner to reconstruct how the outcome was reached. File documentation standards are enforced through supervisory review and periodic quality audits.

items.name: Consumer Complaints
items.summary: Governs the end-to-end handling of policyholder and consumer complaints, turning individual grievances into resolved cases, systemic fixes, and accurate regulatory records.

subs.title: Complaint Tracking
subs.description: All complaints, whether received directly, through producers, or via state insurance departments, are logged in a central system with the complainant, product line, issue category, and handling history. The log distinguishes department-of-insurance complaints from direct complaints, since each carries distinct regulatory handling obligations.

subs.title: Response Timelines
subs.description: Complaints are acknowledged and substantively answered within defined timeframes that meet or exceed each state's requirements, with department-of-insurance inquiries answered by their stated due dates without exception. Approaching deadlines generate automated alerts and unresolved cases are escalated to supervisors.

subs.title: Root Cause Analysis
subs.description: Complaint data is analyzed periodically to identify recurring causes, such as a confusing policy provision, a billing system defect, or a producer conduct pattern, and findings are routed to the owning business area for corrective action. Trends and remediation status are reported to compliance leadership.

subs.title: Regulatory Reporting
subs.description: Complaint records are maintained in the form and detail required for state market conduct annual statement filings and examination requests, and required complaint registers are produced accurately and on time. Data quality checks ensure reported figures reconcile to the tracking system.

items.name: Sales Practice Standards
items.summary: Establishes the conduct rules for how the carrier's products are sold, protecting consumers from unsuitable recommendations and incomplete information while protecting the company from market conduct findings and producer liability.

subs.title: Suitability Requirements
subs.description: Recommendations of annuities, life insurance, and other covered products must be grounded in a documented assessment of the consumer's financial situation, objectives, and needs, consistent with the NAIC suitability and best interest standards adopted in each state. Suitability documentation is captured at point of sale and reviewed before the transaction is accepted.

subs.title: Disclosure Standards
subs.description: Consumers must receive required disclosures at the prescribed points in the sales process, including buyer's guides, policy summaries, illustration certifications, and replacement notices where applicable, in clear language and approved formats. Sales materials and disclosures are subject to advertising review before use.

subs.title: Supervision Requirements
subs.description: A supervisory system monitors producer sales activity through transaction review, replacement and lapse pattern analysis, and complaint signals, with defined escalation when red flags appear. Supervisory responsibilities, review evidence, and disciplinary outcomes are documented to demonstrate effective oversight of both captive and independent distribution.

items.name: Policy Exceptions
items.summary: Controls how departures from corporate policy are requested and granted, ensuring exceptions are deliberate, bounded, and compensated for rather than becoming silent erosions of the control environment.

subs.title: Exception Request Process
subs.description: Any deviation from an approved corporate policy must be requested through the formal exception process, documenting the policy provision affected, the business justification, the risk introduced, and the requested duration. Verbal or undocumented exceptions are not recognized, and operating outside policy without an approved exception is treated as a compliance violation.

subs.title: Approval Authority
subs.description: Exception requests are decided by the designated approval authority, which scales with the risk involved, ranging from the policy owner for low-risk deviations to the relevant executive or risk committee for exceptions with material regulatory or financial exposure. Approvers may not authorize exceptions to policies for which they are the requesting party.

subs.title: Time-Limited
subs.description: Every approved exception carries an explicit expiration date, after which the business must either return to compliance or submit a fresh request with updated justification. Standing or open-ended exceptions are prohibited, and the exception register is reviewed regularly to catch items approaching expiry.

subs.title: Compensating Controls
subs.description: Where an exception weakens a control objective, the approval must identify compensating controls that hold residual risk within tolerance for the exception's duration, such as added monitoring, secondary review, or restricted scope. The effectiveness of compensating controls is validated as part of granting and renewing the exception.

items.name: Policy Management
items.summary: Provides the governance discipline for the corporate policy library itself, ensuring every policy is known, owned, current, and traceable through its revision history.

subs.title: Policy Inventory
subs.description: A complete inventory of all corporate policies is maintained in a central repository, recording each policy's title, owner, applicable business areas, regulatory drivers, and review status. The inventory is the authoritative catalog; policies not registered in it are not recognized as effective.

subs.title: Owner Assigned
subs.description: Each policy has a designated owner of appropriate seniority who is accountable for its content, its alignment with current regulation and business practice, and the timeliness of its reviews. Ownership is reassigned promptly upon departures or reorganizations so no policy is left orphaned.

subs.title: Review Cycle (Annual Minimum)
subs.description: Every policy is reviewed no less than annually, and sooner when regulatory change, audit findings, or operational shifts make its content stale. Reviews confirm continued accuracy and relevance, and the review date, reviewer, and outcome are recorded in the inventory.

subs.title: Version Control
subs.description: Policy documents are maintained under version control that preserves prior versions, records what changed and who approved it, and ensures only the current approved version is published to employees. Historical versions remain retrievable to support examinations, litigation holds, and investigations into past conduct.

items.name: Examination Management
items.summary: Governs how the company prepares for and conducts itself during financial and market conduct examinations, ensuring regulator interactions are organized, responsive, and consistent across the many state jurisdictions in which the carrier operates.

subs.title: Exam Prep Protocol
subs.description: A documented protocol governs readiness for state insurance department examinations, designating an exam coordinator, briefing affected business areas, staging commonly requested materials, and conducting readiness reviews in known problem areas before fieldwork begins. The protocol covers financial, market conduct, and targeted exams alike.

subs.title: Document Request Tracking
subs.description: Every examiner request is logged with its receipt date, assigned owner, due date, and delivery status, giving the exam coordinator a single view of outstanding items. Productions are quality-checked for completeness and responsiveness before release, and a record of exactly what was provided is retained.

subs.title: Response Review Process
subs.description: Written responses to examiner inquiries, draft findings, and report comments undergo review by compliance and, where warranted, legal counsel before submission, ensuring accuracy, consistency with prior representations, and appropriate tone. Significant proposed responses, particularly those contesting findings, require sign-off at a designated senior level.

items.name: Regulatory Change Management
items.summary: Ensures new and amended laws, regulations, and regulatory guidance affecting the carrier are detected early, understood, and implemented before their effective dates, preventing compliance gaps from regulatory movement across fifty-plus jurisdictions.

subs.title: Regulatory Alerts Monitored
subs.description: Designated staff monitor legislative activity, NAIC model law developments, state bulletins, and federal rulemaking through subscription services and regulator channels, capturing relevant items in a change log. Each alert is triaged for applicability to the company's licensed lines and jurisdictions within a defined intake window.

subs.title: Impact Assessments Performed
subs.description: Applicable regulatory changes receive a documented impact assessment identifying affected products, processes, systems, forms, and policies, the compliance deadline, and the scale of effort required. Assessments are completed with enough lead time for the business to plan implementation ahead of the effective date.

subs.title: Implementation Tracked
subs.description: Required changes are assigned to accountable business owners with milestones tracked through to completion, including system updates, form refilings, procedure revisions, and staff training. Status is reported to compliance leadership, and items at risk of missing their regulatory effective date are escalated for intervention.

items.name: Regulatory Findings
items.summary: Governs the remediation of issues raised by regulators, ensuring examination findings and enforcement matters are not merely answered but resolved at their source and prevented from recurring.

subs.title: Findings Tracked to Closure
subs.description: Every finding from an examination, inquiry, or enforcement action is entered into the regulatory issue register with an accountable owner, corrective action plan, and committed completion date, and remains open until remediation is verified, not merely reported. Closure requires evidence sufficient to demonstrate the fix to the regulator if requested.

subs.title: Root Cause Analysis
subs.description: Each significant finding undergoes analysis to determine the underlying cause, distinguishing isolated execution errors from defects in process design, system logic, training, or oversight. The analysis is documented and shapes the corrective action so the response addresses the cause rather than the symptom.

subs.title: Preventive Measures
subs.description: Beyond correcting the specific instance cited, remediation must include measures that prevent recurrence, such as control enhancements, monitoring additions, or procedure and training changes, applied across all business units and jurisdictions where the same condition could exist. The effectiveness of preventive measures is checked through subsequent compliance testing.

items.name: Regulatory Inventory
items.summary: Maintains the authoritative map of the legal and regulatory obligations that apply to the enterprise, giving the compliance function a complete basis for assigning accountability and detecting when obligations shift.

subs.title: Applicable Regulations Catalogued
subs.description: All laws, regulations, and binding guidance applicable to the company's licensed entities, product lines, and jurisdictions are catalogued in a structured inventory, spanning state insurance codes, NAIC model adoptions, and applicable federal requirements such as privacy and anti-money laundering rules. Each entry records the obligation's substance and the business activities it touches.

subs.title: Ownership Assigned
subs.description: Every catalogued obligation is mapped to a business or compliance owner responsible for ensuring the company's processes and controls satisfy it. Ownership mappings are validated periodically so coverage gaps created by reorganizations or new products are caught and reassigned.

subs.title: Changes Tracked
subs.description: The inventory is updated as regulations are adopted, amended, or repealed, drawing on the regulatory change management process, with each entry's revision history preserved. Updates trigger notification to the assigned owner so downstream policies, procedures, and controls are revisited.

items.name: Regulatory Reporting
items.summary: Governs the production and submission of the company's required regulatory filings, ensuring statutory statements, data calls, and other submissions are complete, accurate, on time, and retrievable afterward.

subs.title: Filing Inventory
subs.description: A master inventory lists every required regulatory filing across all jurisdictions and licensed entities, including statutory financial statements, market conduct annual statements, premium tax returns, and state data calls, with each filing's frequency, due date, preparer, and reviewer. New obligations identified through regulatory change management are added before their first due date.

subs.title: Accuracy Controls
subs.description: Filings are subject to defined preparation controls, including reconciliation of reported figures to source systems and the general ledger, independent review by someone other than the preparer, and sign-off by the accountable officer where attestation is required. Errors discovered post-submission are corrected through the prescribed amendment process and analyzed for cause.

subs.title: Timely Submission
subs.description: Each filing must be submitted on or before its regulatory deadline, with the calendar of due dates monitored and internal milestones set ahead of each deadline to absorb preparation slippage. Anticipated delays are escalated early enough to request extensions where the jurisdiction permits, and any late filing is logged and reported to compliance leadership.

subs.title: Retention Requirements
subs.description: Submitted filings, supporting workpapers, and evidence of submission are retained in accordance with the corporate retention schedule and applicable state requirements, in a form that allows prompt retrieval during examinations or inquiries. Retention applies equally to superseded and amended versions so the full filing history is preserved.

items.name: Third-Party Risk Management
items.summary: Establishes the lifecycle controls for risk arising from vendors and other third parties, recognizing that outsourced functions such as TPAs, IT providers, and data processors carry the carrier's regulatory and reputational exposure with them.

subs.title: Vendor Due Diligence
subs.description: Prospective vendors undergo risk-proportionate due diligence before engagement, evaluating financial stability, information security posture, regulatory and licensing status, business continuity capability, and use of subcontractors. Due diligence results are documented and must support an approval decision before contracts are executed or data is shared.

subs.title: Risk Tiering
subs.description: Each third party is assigned a risk tier based on criteria such as access to nonpublic personal information, performance of regulated functions like claims administration, criticality to operations, and concentration exposure. The tier drives the depth of due diligence, contract provisions, and ongoing monitoring applied to the relationship.

subs.title: Ongoing Monitoring
subs.description: Active vendor relationships are monitored on a cadence set by their risk tier, including periodic reassessments, review of SOC reports and security attestations, performance against service levels, and tracking of vendor incidents and breaches. Deteriorating vendors are escalated, with remediation required or exit plans invoked when risk exceeds tolerance.

subs.title: Contract Requirements
subs.description: Vendor contracts must include the protective provisions appropriate to the relationship's risk tier, such as confidentiality and data protection obligations, breach notification timeframes, audit and examination rights extending to insurance regulators, subcontracting restrictions, and termination remedies. Contract templates are maintained with legal, and deviations from required clauses follow the exception process.
